opening.notes: The answer is real (F# E# F# C# D C# F# C# | C# B G# B B A G# A ...), an 11th below, exact to 4:3.75; its last beat is varied (eighths A2 B2 for the sixteenths) and it lands on C#3 at 5:1. The bass is a non-thematic continuo line until its own entry. The end of the solo subject at 3:1 (bass G2 to F#2 under the right hand's F#4) is a half close on V, but it is the subject's own ending, not counted as a cadence.

notes: Fugal in layout: a subject alone over a continuo bass, a real answer at the dominant with a countersubject, a third entry (right hand, f#) exchanging the pair, an episode, entries in D and A, an episode, and two entries in the tonic in overlap, with the countersubject kept throughout (invertible at the octave). Form call unsure: rounded bipartite reads the PAC in D at 12:1 as the central cadence (III) with the tonic return at 18:1.5; the alternative is tripartite (1-5:3, 5:3-12:1, 12:1-22; the second section begins with x in f#), with sections of 4.5, 6.5 and 10 bars. The arrival on e at 16:1 (B7 over F# to E in the bass, with A in the right hand) is not counted as a cadence: the expected landing of x is replaced by the episode. About 12 of 22 bars are paradigm members, plus the opening solo statement.
